76503-the-man-who-mastered-time.title: The Man Who Mastered Time
76503-the-man-who-mastered-time.creator: Unknown
76503-the-man-who-mastered-time.description: A public-domain book from Project Gutenberg. "  Rogers gazed earnestly about the room. Those are the three factors which make up our universe as we know it. I said they were blended. I mean that the actual reality underlying all the manifestations we experience is not temporal or spatial or material, but a blend of all three. It is we who, in our minds, have split up the original unity into three such supposedly different things as time, space and matter."  "Take space and time," said the Big Business Man.

arxiv-2212-02428.title: Using the SourceXtractor++ package for data reduction
arxiv-2212-02428.creator: M. Kümmel, A. Álvarez-Ayllón, E. Bertin, P. Dubath, R. Gavazzi, W. Hartley, M. Schefer, on behalf of the Euclid Consortium
arxiv-2212-02428.description: Abstract The Euclid satellite is an ESA mission scheduled for launch in September 2023. To optimally perform critical stages of the data reduction, such as object detection and morphology determination, a new and modern software package was required. We have developed SourceXtractor++ as open source software for detecting and measuring sources in astronomical images.

arxiv-2212-12700.title: JDNN: Jacobi Deep Neural Network for Solving Telegraph Equation Journal: Journal of L a T e X Templates
arxiv-2212-12700.creator: Maryam Babaei, Kimia Mohammadi Mohammadi, Zeinab Hajimohammadi, Kourosh Parand
arxiv-2212-12700.description: Abstract In this article, a new deep learning architecture, named JDNN, has been proposed to approximate a numerical solution to Partial Differential Equations (PDEs). The JDNN is capable of solving high-dimensional equations. Here, Jacobi Deep Neural Network (JDNN) has demonstrated various types of telegraph equations.

arxiv-2305-06182.title: The Cauchy problem for the (2+1) integrable nonlinear Schrödinger equation
arxiv-2305-06182.creator: L. P. Nizhnik
arxiv-2305-06182.description: Abstract We study the Cauchy problem for the (2+1) integrable nonlinear Schrödinger equation by the inverse scattering transform (IST) method. This Cauchy problem with given initial data and boundary data at infinity is reduced by IST to the Cauchy problem for the linear Schrödinger equation, in which the potential is expressed in terms of boundary data.

arxiv-2404-15654.title: Autoregressive Networks with Dependent Edges
arxiv-2404-15654.creator: Jinyuan Chang, Qin Fang, Eric D. Kolaczyk, Peter W. MacDonald, Qiwei Yao
arxiv-2404-15654.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Jinyuan Chang, Qin Fang, Eric D. Kolaczyk, Peter W. MacDonald, Qiwei Yao. We propose an autoregressive framework for modelling dynamic networks with dependent edges. It encompasses models that accommodate, for example, transitivity, degree heterogenenity, and other stylized features often observed in real network data. By assuming the edges of networks at each time are independent conditionally on their lagged values, the models, which exhibit a close connection with temporal ERGMs, facilitate both simulation and the maximum likelihood estimation in a straightforward manner.

arxiv-2406-06120.title: Harmonically trapped inertial run-and-tumble particle in one dimension
arxiv-2406-06120.creator: Debraj Dutta, Anupam Kundu, Sanjib Sabhapandit, Urna Basu
arxiv-2406-06120.description: Abstract We study the nonequilibrium stationary state of a one-dimensional inertial run-and-tumble particle (IRTP) trapped in a harmonic potential. We find that the presence of inertia leads to two distinct dynamical scenarios, namely, overdamped and underdamped, characterized by the relative strength of the viscous and the trap time-scales.

arxiv-2408-03437.title: Learning Global Linear Representations of Nonlinear Dynamics
arxiv-2408-03437.creator: Thomas Breunung †, Florian Kogelbauer
arxiv-2408-03437.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Thomas Breunung †, Florian Kogelbauer. While linear systems are well-understood, no explicit solution for general nonlinear systems exists. A classical approach to make the understanding of linear system available in the nonlinear setting is to represent a nonlinear system by a linear model. While progress has been made in extending linearization techniques to larger domains and more complex attractor geometries, recent work has highlighted the limitations of these techniques when applied to nonlinear dynamics, such as those with coexisting attractors.

arxiv-2411-18686.title: Convective mixing in distant and close-in giant planets
arxiv-2411-18686.creator: J. Polman, C. Mordasini
arxiv-2411-18686.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by J. Polman, C. Mordasini. Recent structure models of Jupiter suggest the existence of an extended region in the deep interior with a high heavy element abundance, referred to as a dilute core. This finding has led to increased interest in modelling the formation and evolution processes with the goal of understanding how and under what circumstances such a structure is formed and retained, to in turn better understand the relation between atmospheric and bulk metallicity.

pmc-10490972.creator: Diana Naranjo, Elisabeth Kimball, Jeanette Nelson, Matthew Samore, Stephen C. Alder, Kevin Stroupe, Charlesnika T. Evans, Frances M. Weaver, Cara Ray, Ibuola Kale, Patrick O. Galyean, Susan Zickmund, Andrea Cioffi, Andrea Cioffi, Andrea Cioffi

pmc-10507117.creator: Sabine Dritz, Rebecca A Nelson, Fernanda S Valdovinos
pmc-10507117.description: Understanding the assembly of plant-pollinator communities has become critical to their conservation given the rise of species invasions, extirpations, and species’ range shifts. Over the course of assembly, colonizer establishment produces core interaction patterns, called motifs, which shape the trajectory of assembling network structure.

pmc-11435345.title: Ultraviolet Light-Induced Surface Changes of Tungsten Oxide in Air: Combined Scanning Transmission Electron Microscopy and X-ray Photoelectron Spectroscopy Analysis
pmc-11435345.creator: Yuki Nakagawa, Yasuhiro Shiratsuchi, Tamaki Shibayama, Masaki Takeguchi, Detlef W Bahnemann
pmc-11435345.description: Scanning transmission electron microscopy (STEM) and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy analyses were combined to clarify the ultraviolet light-induced surface changes of WO3 in air. Identical-location STEM (IL-STEM) analysis showed that the WO3 particle surface was covered with an amorphous thin film after ultraviolet irradiation in air. X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy analysis showed that hydrocarbon decomposition and the formation of carboxyl/hydroxyl species occurred.

pmc-11540067.title: A retrospective cohort study on the protective effect of influenza vaccination during pregnancy in Gansu Province
pmc-11540067.creator: Xue-Feng Liang, Juan-Xia Peng, Di Sun, Bing-Ling Zhang, Jing An, Xiao-Shu Zhang
pmc-11540067.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). To evaluate the Vaccine Effectiveness (VE) of the Influenza Vaccine (InfV) during pregnancy in Gansu province. A retrospective cohort of pregnant women vaccinated with InfV was constructed using the electronic case system and immunization planning system of Gansu province. Outcome information of Influenza-Like Illness (ILI) in pregnant women after vaccination with InfV during the influenza epidemic seasons from 2019 to 2021 was collected. The log-binomial model was used to estimate the adjusted Risk Ratio (RR), VE, and their Confidence Intervals (CI).

pmc-11639974.title: Effect of Feeding Sugarcane Bagasse-Extracted Polyphenolic Mixture on the Growth Performance, Meat Quality, and Oxidative and Inflammatory Status of Chronic Heat-Stressed Broiler Chickens
pmc-11639974.creator: Motoi Kikusato, Fu Namai, Katsushige Yamada, Mingliang Jin, Velmurugu Ravindran
pmc-11639974.description: Simple SummaryThe management of heat stress (HS) in domestic animals has been an important issue for sustainable meat production in the era of accelerated global warming. Chickens are more susceptible to high temperatures than other livestock animals because they lack sweat glands and heat dissipation is limited to the face, legs, and comb, which are not covered with feathers.

pmc-11712422.title: Implication of Chronotherapy in mouse models of Alzheimer’s Disease
pmc-11712422.creator: Yu Shi, Ricardo Salinas, William McRoberts, Stephen Rozen, Jordan Swint, George S Bloom, Ali Güler
pmc-11712422.description: BackgroundSleep disturbances are commonly observed in early‐stage Alzheimer’s Disease (AD) patients and correlate with their cognitive performance over time. Sleep in mammals is governed by the central circadian system, which responds to environmental cues like light and aligns with daily routines such as eating.

pmc-13547587.title: Telenursing to Improve Quality of Life in Women With Breast Cancer: A Systematic Review and Meta‐Analysis
pmc-13547587.creator: Serena Ricchiuto, Diego Lopane, Stefano Mancin, Daniela Cattani, Alessandra Dacomi, Simone Cosmai, Mattia Bozzetti, Beatrice Mazzoleni
pmc-13547587.description: BackgroundBreast cancer is the most commonly diagnosed malignancy in women and a leading cause of cancer‐related mortality. Beyond the physical burden, the disease significantly impacts emotional well‐being and quality of life (QoL). Telenursing, as a nurse‐led telemedicine intervention, has emerged as a promising strategy to support patients remotely.

pmc-13586580.title: From pixels to conservation: Deep learning for automated monitoring of rare and endangered wildlife
pmc-13586580.creator: Donghua Xuan, Yuchen Cai, Minxi Xu, Chao Long, Nian Cai
pmc-13586580.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). SummaryConservation of rare and endangered species requires scalable monitoring solutions to address accelerating biodiversity loss. Deep learning has transformed wildlife monitoring, enabling automated species identification, individual tracking, demographic inference, and behavioral analysis from camera traps, drones, and video surveillance. This review systematically analyzes 159 wildlife monitoring studies (2014–2026) across four technical domains: species recognition, individual re-identification, soft biometrics (age/sex estimation), and behavior/pose analysis.

uslaw-usc-t25-s342.title: 25 U.S.C. § 342 — Removal of Southern Utes to new reservation
uslaw-usc-t25-s342.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t25-s342.description: United States Code, Title 25 (Indians); Chapter 9 (Allotment Of Indian Lands). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. Nothing in this act shall be so construed as to prevent the removal of the Southern Ute Indians from their present reservation in southwestern Colorado to a new reservation by and with the consent of a majority of the adult male members of said tribe.
